# Selected result: a quantum link through a fixed, lossy measurement port

**Can a fixed measurement interaction support arbitrarily accurate quantum communication after its original carrier is discarded, even when almost all emitted light is lost—and what must that loss cost?**

I select this question. The construction below answers it for the driven dephasing source
\[
H_S=\frac{\Omega}{2}X,\qquad L_S=\sqrt{\gamma}\,Z,
\]
with vacuum input and coherent collection efficiency \(\eta\).

The completed result is:

> **For every fixed \(\gamma>0\), \(\Omega\ne0\), and emission duration \(T>0\), the initial-qubit-to-collected-field channel satisfies**
> \[
> \boxed{Q_{\leftrightarrow}(\mathcal N_{\eta,T})=\Theta(\eta)}
> \qquad(\eta\downarrow0).
> \]
> **A finite chronological receiver, local filters, and explicit entanglement purification attain the lower bound. The receiver dimension is independent of \(\eta\). At \(\Omega=0\), the channel is entanglement breaking and its two-way assisted quantum capacity is zero.**

Here \(Q_{\leftrightarrow}\) counts reliably transmitted qubits per fixed-duration source window, allowing local quantum operations and classical communication. The final source is discarded.

The operational change is consequential: **generate and purify shared entanglement first; introduce the unknown payload afterward and teleport it.** This requires a retained memory at Alice, local preparation of a source–memory Bell pair, and local processing at both ends. It does not recover an already inaccessible unknown source state.

That distinction earns an actual capability: nodes with suitable local quantum operations can communicate through this native measurement interaction without programming the source to emit a state-transfer waveform. A finite-cavity calculation also gives a concrete operating point at **1% collection**, with certified raw Bell fidelity above **0.89420**. The rates obtained here are conservative and do not establish an engineering advantage over purpose-built quantum interconnects.

## 1. The comparison changes the operation we construct

My earlier decoding opening completed its inference-to-matching chain under an independent graphlike fault representation. It did not acquire a comparable representation for general correlated circuit noise. I select the interface route because its central operation can be completed more fully.

The peer’s construction makes the relevant distinction especially clear. Its two captures assemble a complete Pauli operator basis, allowing direct transfer of an already unknown input. Loss can corrupt that input before a successful receiver flag appears. Repeating a failed experiment cannot recover the same unknown state.

This is a fundamental obstruction in the stated Markov model, rather than merely a weakness of the peer’s receiver.

### A quantitative obstruction to direct recovery

Let
\[
\lambda=(1-\eta)\gamma>0.
\]
For any receiver-only protocol, with initially independent ancillas, no source feedback, and an inaccessible reference, let \(p\) be its success probability on a Bell input and \(F_e\) its conditional entanglement fidelity. Then
\[
\boxed{
1-F_e\ge
\frac{e^{-1/4}}{64}
\frac{\lambda}{|\Omega|+\lambda}\sqrt p .
}
\tag{1}
\]

Thus exact heralded recovery has zero success probability when collection loss is nonzero. At fixed source parameters, arbitrarily accurate direct recovery forces \(p=O((1-F_e)^2)\).

The load-bearing argument concerns an unobserved early lost photon. A lost jump applies \(Z\). It commutes with the retained-field coupling and reverses only the bounded drive Hamiltonian. Moving a lost jump at time \(t\) to the beginning therefore changes the normalized evolution by at most \(|\Omega|t\).

Absorb all subsequent evolution and successful receiver processing into a common contraction \(K\). For an initial interval of length \(a\), let \(s_0\) be the accepted norm squared with no lost jump in that interval, and \(g_0\) its correct-Bell component. Writing \(\delta=1-F_e\),
\[
p\le(\sqrt{s_0}+|\Omega|a)^2,
\qquad
g_0\ge s_0-e^{\lambda a}p\delta .
\]
A lost \(Z\) moves the correct Bell component into an orthogonal Bell subspace. The exactly-one-lost-jump trajectories consequently imply
\[
p\delta\ge
\lambda e^{-\lambda a}
\int_0^a
\bigl(\sqrt{g_0}-|\Omega|t\bigr)_+^2\,dt .
\]
Choosing \(a=\sqrt p/[4(|\Omega|+\lambda)]\) gives (1). The bound permits state-dependent heralding.
